newsitem.title: LEBANON: BLC up, Solidere mixed on Beirut exchange.
newsitem.headline: BLC up, Solidere mixed on Beirut exchange.

text.p: Shares of Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose on Tuesday on the Beirut Stock Exchange, continuing a rally since its first listing on the market more than two weeks ago.
BLC shares rose more than one percent to $12.375 from Monday's $12.25 on trade of 5,000 shares against 6,063 shares.

BLC is the first commercial bank to list on the Beirut exchange since the market reopened in January 1995. Its shares have risen steadily since listing on the market on December 30 and closing that day at $11.25.
Dealers have said that there is a lot of demand for the bank's shares but that market makers are executing the orders slowly to avoid a rapid rise in their price.
Also on the Beirut stock exchange, Solidere A shares rose to $11.125 from $11 on Monday and B shares fell to $11.375 from $11.50.
Turnover in Solidere fell sharply to 15,880 shares from 62,400 shares on Monday and value was $177,757.5 from $683,468.75.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index rose 0.13 percent to 81.92 and the BLOM stock index fell 0.03 percent to 941.64.
